703.name: Gnat Skiff
703.desc: The cheapest thing in any shipyard that can still jump. A cockpit, a cargo nook, one blaster, and a reputation for outliving the pilots who mock it.

704.name: Dory Hauler
704.desc: A slab-sided box with engines bolted on. Every independent freight family has started with a Dory. Slow, ugly, and it carries a surprising amount.

705.name: Kestrel Scout
705.desc: A swept-wing scout built for system patrols and fast courier work. It is quick, nimble and paper-thin.

706.name: Mule Tender
706.desc: A boxy tender with modular cargo pods and a big fuel reserve. The Lamplighters use them to keep beacons running out where no one else bothers to go.

707.name: Wayfarer
707.desc: A long-legged explorer with ringed fuel collectors and room for a crew to live in. It can run a dozen jumps without stopping to refuel.

708.name: Cutlass Interceptor
708.desc: A blade of a ship: blended wing, forward guns, and engines almost too big for it. Popular with bounty hunters and, unfortunately, with raiders.

709.name: Lacewing Sail Yacht
709.desc: A rich pilot's toy: shimmering solar sails that feed its tanks and a hull built for speed and nothing else. Fast enough to outrun almost anything.

710.name: Ore Crawler
710.desc: An armored mining rig with forward grapple-arms, an ore hopper and a Seam Tapper. It is slow and tough, and pays for itself in a few good asteroid fields.

711.name: Bramble Gunboat
711.desc: A hull bristling with turrets. Bramble crews joke that they never need to aim, only to face the right part of the sky.

712.name: Longhaul Barge
712.desc: Three cargo modules on a spine, with a bridge at one end and engines at the other. It's the backbone of independent bulk trade.

713.name: Halberd Frigate
713.desc: A well-armed frigate with deep magazines, the sort of ship a planetary militia orders by the dozen.

714.name: Pilgrim Liner
714.desc: A gleaming passenger liner with long rows of lit windows and a lot of room. Its captains do brisk business carrying pilgrims, refugees and anyone else with a ticket.

715.name: Hive Tender
715.desc: A drone carrier. Its hex-pod hangars launch swarms of Mite drones, and one Hive can keep a whole system's raiders busy.

716.name: Tempest Destroyer
716.desc: A black-hulled destroyer that is fast for its size and terrifying head-on. Very few civilians can afford one, and the ones who can usually don't say where the money came from.

717.name: Bastion Dreadnought
717.desc: A slow armored fortress. Shipyards build one when an order comes in, and orders don't come in often.

718.name: Mite Drone
718.desc: A tiny fearless drone fighter launched from a Mite Drone Bay.

720.name: Gnat Skiff Mk II
720.desc: A Gnat Skiff refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

721.name: Kestrel Scout Mk II
721.desc: A Kestrel Scout refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

722.name: Dory Hauler Mk II
722.desc: A Dory Hauler refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

723.name: Cutlass Interceptor Mk II
723.desc: A Cutlass Interceptor refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

724.name: Mule Tender Mk II
724.desc: A Mule Tender refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

725.name: Wayfarer Mk II
725.desc: A Wayfarer refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

726.name: Lacewing Sail Yacht Mk II
726.desc: A Lacewing Sail Yacht refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

727.name: Ore Crawler Mk II
727.desc: A Ore Crawler refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

728.name: Bramble Gunboat Mk II
728.desc: A Bramble Gunboat refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

729.name: Longhaul Barge Mk II
729.desc: A Longhaul Barge refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

730.name: Halberd Frigate Mk II
730.desc: A Halberd Frigate refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

731.name: Pilgrim Liner Mk II
731.desc: A Pilgrim Liner refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

732.name: Hive Tender Mk II
732.desc: A Hive Tender refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

733.name: Tempest Destroyer Mk II
733.desc: A Tempest Destroyer refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

734.name: Bastion Dreadnought Mk II
734.desc: A Bastion Dreadnought refit at Quantum Station's drydock: reinforced hull, upgraded shield emitters, retuned drives, extra outfit space, and the station's gold refit stripe.

735.name: Halo Surveyor
735.desc: A wide survey disc with twin boosters slung close beneath it. The Halo was built to go a long way, look carefully at everything, and come home again: huge fuel reserves, a sensor mast as standard, and a ring of observation windows around the rim. It can defend itself, but it would rather not.

736.name: Concordance
736.desc:
CONCORDANCE CLASS. A vast blue armored command hull bristling with turret batteries, with twin pontoons slung low and aft on angled struts. Fewer than a dozen have ever been laid down, and every one of them has a name people speak quietly.

The most expensive ship a private captain can buy, and one of the largest.

Standard armament: eight Kiln Bastions, four Spall Drivers, four quantum torpedo tubes, six Ember flak turrets, twin Lantern Lances, twin Snare projectors and four Wisp rocket pods.

The Concordance enters hyperspace without slowing down, and Quantum Station's drydock can fit her with a Warp Spine that takes a whole plotted route in one warp.

737.name: Lumen Mote
737.desc: A tiny Que'vari sail-dart launched from a Mote Bay: a single sail, a single emitter, and no fear at all.

738.name: Glimmer
738.desc: The smallest true Que'vari sail-ship: a pearl-white needle with three spread electro-sails. Que'vari children learn to fly in Glimmers, and then never quite want to stop.

739.name: Sunwake Sloop
739.desc: A broad, gentle trader with twin cargo pods and two fanned sail-masts. Sunwakes carry most of the Que'vari's trade, and their crews sing while they work.

740.name: Prism Corvette
740.desc: An arrowhead warship with a living prism set in its prow. Prism Corvettes guard the sail-lanes in pairs.

741.name: Aureate Frigate
741.desc: A long pearl hull ringed with gold emitter bands and four great electro-sails. Aureates are the backbone of the Que'vari choirs-of-war.

742.name: Radiance Cruiser
742.desc: A cruiser built around a spinal prism lance, its six sails fanned like the wings of something holy. When a Radiance arrives, the Umbral leave.

743.name: Choir Carrier
743.desc: Twin hulls joined by a glowing flight deck, crowned with an arc of seven sails. A Choir launches its Motes in waves, and they sing as they go.

744.name: Ina Que'var
744.desc:
THE INA QUE'VAR. The great sail-ship of the People of Light: a vast, whale-shaped hull carrying a forest of light-blue electro-sails, driven by beams of light that stream from her emitters like a comet's tail. There is only one, and the Que'vari do not build another.

Standard armament: ten Sail Lances, six Prism Shard Cannons, four Corona Torpedo tubes and eight Halo Burst turrets. Her sails also slowly refill her fuel.

745.name: Cutlass Interceptor Mk III
745.desc: The Cutlass Interceptor rebuilt at Quantum Station's Station Tier 5 drydock: obsidian armor plate, quantum conduits glowing along the hull, twin auxiliary drive pods, an extra hardpoint, self-repairing armor and much more room for outfits. Only a Mk II can be taken this far.

746.name: Halberd Frigate Mk III
746.desc: The Halberd Frigate rebuilt at Quantum Station's Station Tier 5 drydock: obsidian armor plate, quantum conduits glowing along the hull, twin auxiliary drive pods, an extra hardpoint, self-repairing armor and much more room for outfits. Only a Mk II can be taken this far.

747.name: Bramble Gunboat Mk III
747.desc: The Bramble Gunboat rebuilt at Quantum Station's Station Tier 5 drydock: obsidian armor plate, quantum conduits glowing along the hull, twin auxiliary drive pods, an extra hardpoint, self-repairing armor and much more room for outfits. Only a Mk II can be taken this far.

748.name: Hive Tender Mk III
748.desc: The Hive Tender rebuilt at Quantum Station's Station Tier 5 drydock: obsidian armor plate, quantum conduits glowing along the hull, twin auxiliary drive pods, an extra hardpoint, self-repairing armor and much more room for outfits. Only a Mk II can be taken this far.

749.name: Tempest Destroyer Mk III
749.desc: The Tempest Destroyer rebuilt at Quantum Station's Station Tier 5 drydock: obsidian armor plate, quantum conduits glowing along the hull, twin auxiliary drive pods, an extra hardpoint, self-repairing armor and much more room for outfits. Only a Mk II can be taken this far.

750.name: Bastion Dreadnought Mk III
750.desc: The Bastion Dreadnought rebuilt at Quantum Station's Station Tier 5 drydock: obsidian armor plate, quantum conduits glowing along the hull, twin auxiliary drive pods, an extra hardpoint, self-repairing armor and much more room for outfits. Only a Mk II can be taken this far.

751.name: Sable Okoro
751.desc: Sable's own Nightjar: a forward-swept night scout in slate and teal, with sensor vanes that pick out raiders before they pick you out. She built it from three wrecks and a courier contract.
751.pilot:
WINGMATE: SABLE OKORO

Sable flew courier runs through raider space for six years and never lost a package. She scouts ahead, calls targets early, and laughs at her own jokes over the comm.

Ship: the Nightjar, a one-of-a-kind night scout.

752.name: Brannock Teague
752.desc: Brannock's Hound: a blunt armored brawler with two heavy cannons as long as the hull and a red stripe where the bounty license used to be. It goes straight for whatever is shooting at you, and it does not stop.
752.pilot:
WINGMATE: BRANNOCK TEAGUE

A former bounty hunter with a Cutlass he rebuilt twice. Brannock goes straight for whatever is shooting at you.

Ship: the Hound, a one-of-a-kind bounty brawler.

753.name: Ines Varro
753.desc: Ines's Covenant: a white-and-blue escort frigate ringed with great shield emitters, built to put itself between you and the guns. Seven turrets, and every one of them answers to her.
753.pilot:
WINGMATE: INES VARRO

A militia frigate captain who resigned rather than fire on a refugee convoy. Steady, precise, and unshakably loyal.

Ship: the Covenant, a one-of-a-kind escort frigate.

754.name: Old Mags Pell
754.desc: The Thornback: a squat round gun-platform bristling with ten turrets and thirty years of patch plates. Mags says nothing gets close to you, and she has never once been wrong.
754.pilot:
WINGMATE: OLD MAGS PELL

Mags has flown the same turret-heavy Bramble for thirty years and says she will be buried in it. Nothing gets close to you.

Ship: the Thornback, a one-of-a-kind gun platform.

755.name: Juniper Hale
755.desc: Juniper's Swiftsure: a twin-boom racer in race orange and white that is mostly engine. It holds three academy speed records and a fourth that nobody is allowed to talk about.
755.pilot:
WINGMATE: JUNIPER HALE

A yacht racer who got bored of trophies. Juniper is the fastest pilot in the academy and knows it.

Ship: the Swiftsure, a one-of-a-kind racing fighter.

756.name: Tomas Eriksen-Kai
756.desc: Tomas's Lifeline: a long-range rescue ship with a ring of drone cradles and two tractor arms. Its Mite drones swarm anything that threatens you, and it keeps its own armor and fuel topped up.
756.pilot:
WINGMATE: TOMAS ERIKSEN-KAI

A long-range explorer and medic. Tomas keeps his tanks full and his crew calm, and he has pulled more than one pilot out of a dead ship.

Ship: the Lifeline, a one-of-a-kind rescue carrier.

757.name: Armada Frigate
757.desc: A Mk III Halberd and crew on loan from the Quantum Armada. Disciplined, heavily armed, and very expensive.
757.pilot:
ARMADA FRIGATE

A Mk III Halberd and crew on loan from the Quantum Armada. Disciplined, heavily armed, and very expensive.

758.name: Armada Destroyer
758.desc: A Mk III Tempest from the Quantum Armada, crewed by the academy's best gunners.
758.pilot:
ARMADA DESTROYER

A Mk III Tempest from the Quantum Armada, crewed by the academy's best gunners.

759.name: Armada Carrier
759.desc: A Mk III Hive carrier from the Quantum Armada. Its drone swarms can hold a system on their own.
759.pilot:
ARMADA CARRIER

A Mk III Hive carrier from the Quantum Armada. Its drone swarms can hold a system on their own.

760.name: Umbral Shade
760.desc: A Que'vari Glimmer taken by the Umbral, its sails dyed the color of a bruise and its emitters choked down to a red ember.

761.name: Umbral Hunter
761.desc: A corvette stolen from the Que'vari and turned to the hunt. Umbral Hunters run dark and strike from behind.

762.name: Umbral Reaver
762.desc: A frigate whose sails drink light instead of riding it. Reavers lead Umbral packs.

763.name: Umbral Dread
763.desc: A Radiance cruiser twisted into a dreadnought of the dark. Where a Dread passes, sail-ships fall becalmed.

764.name: The Night Anchor
764.desc: The flagship of the Umbral: a vast Dread hung with shrouds, its sails black as a closed eye.

765.name: Thrip Darter
765.desc: A Vashari thrip: a needle of black chitin on two pairs of membrane wings. It is grown, not built, and it heals its own scratches. Vashari broods launch them in clouds; the rest of the galaxy buys them as the cheapest fast courier on the market.

766.name: Silkspinner Hauler
766.desc: A Vashari freight-bearer: a small armored head pulling a great silk sac that it fills, seals and spins tight. The silk glows faintly where it is stretched.

767.name: Mantis Lancer
767.desc: A raptorial Vashari hunter that folds its forelimbs back along its body and strikes with them like lances. Fast, mean, and very hard to shake off.

768.name: Carapace Destroyer
768.desc: A war-beetle the length of a frigate. Its wing-cases open in battle over glowing membranes, and its chitin knits itself back together between fights.

769.name: Brood Queen
769.desc: A Vashari hive-queen. Her vast egg-sac glows with brood cells, and every few minutes one of them hatches into a Thrip Darter and takes flight.

770.name: Slag Skiff
770.desc: A Korrund mining skiff: a hollowed boulder with a cutting claw and a vent of molten rock for a drive. Almost impossible to break, almost impossible to hurry.

771.name: Basalt Gunboat
771.desc: A stepped wedge of basalt with two long cannon. Korrund gunboats have no shields worth the name; they simply do not care what you shoot at them.

772.name: Magma Hauler
772.desc: A chain of stone cargo blocks bound with glowing bands of magma. It carries ore, it carries anything, and pirates learned long ago that it carries guns.

773.name: Forge Cruiser
773.desc: A floating forge-mountain with a caldera of live magma at its heart. Its crews cast fresh armor plate in the middle of a battle.

774.name: Mountain Dreadnought
774.desc: A whole mountain range, three peaks high, with rivers of lava running down to a ring of cannon towers. The Korrund say a Mountain is not launched, it is moved.

775.name: Glint Scout
775.desc: One long shard of violet crystal and two splinters flying beside it, held in place by a hum you can feel in your teeth. Nothing touches.

776.name: Facet Yacht
776.desc: A crown of crystal shards turning slowly around a white heart. Ylith nobles cross the galaxy in Facets just to be looked at, and their shields are very, very good.

777.name: Lattice Frigate
777.desc: A spearhead of three crystal banks with a lattice of light strung between them. Break a bank loose and the lattice simply pulls it back.

778.name: Resonance Cruiser
778.desc: A great tuning fork of crystal. The gap between its tines sings, and the song is a weapon.

779.name: Cathedral Carrier
779.desc: A cathedral of crystal spires around a hollow nave where Glint Scouts are grown like frost.

780.name: Spoke Runner
780.desc: A single brass wheel with a rider-cab at the hub and a scrap of canvas for a tail. Sarn children race them between the caravans.

781.name: Wheelhouse Trader
781.desc: A spinning hab-wheel on a rusted keel, cargo nets and patched awnings slung on either side. A Sarn family lives aboard, and so does everything they own.

782.name: Gyre Frigate
782.desc: Twin gun-wheels spinning in opposite directions on outriggers, so the Gyre can fire in every direction at once. The caravans' guardians.

783.name: Caravan Liner
783.desc: A train of hab-wheels strung along a spine, every lantern lit. Passengers pay for the trip and stay for the music.

784.name: Grand Caravan
784.desc: A city on wheels: a market hub inside a great outer ring of stalls and homes, with barges in tow. When a Grand Caravan arrives in a system, the system throws a fair.

785.name: Möbius
785.desc:
THE MÖBIUS. EXOTIC. A hull made of one continuous twisted ribbon: it has only one side and only one edge. Walk the corridor far enough and you arrive back where you started, upside down. Nobody knows how it flies this fast, including its builders.

Standard armament: six Paradox Lances. Its drive refills its own fuel, and it enters hyperspace without slowing down.

786.name: Orrery
786.desc:
THE ORRERY. EXOTIC. A captured star in a gimballed cage of brass rings, with six worldlets riding the rings like beads. Each worldlet holds a district of the ship; the star powers everything, refuels everything, and slowly mends the armor.

Standard armament: six Gravity Wells and two Paradox Lances.

787.name: Event Horizon
787.desc:
THE EVENT HORIZON. EXOTIC. A ship built around a black hole on a leash. The hull is the accretion disk, the drive is the jets, and the armor is whatever the gravity has not let go of. Its Singularity Torpedo needs no ammunition: it is a small piece of the hole, thrown.

Standard armament: a Singularity Torpedo and four Gravity Wells.

788.name: Vespid Frigate
788.desc: A Vashari war-wasp, thin-waisted and banded in glowing green, with a stinger that is mostly decoration and a temper that is not. The backbone of every Vashari swarm.

789.name: Stagback Dreadnought
789.desc: A stag beetle the size of a station, its branching antlers longer than most frigates. The Vashari grow one a generation, and the whole swarm follows it.

790.name: Ember Dart
790.desc: A glowing shard of slag thrown from an Anvil carrier, with one cannon and one vent. Korrund fighter pilots are said to be the only Korrund in a hurry.

791.name: Cinder Frigate
791.desc: Three stone wedges stacked like a stair, with cannon pods on either flank and a keel of running magma. It does not dodge.

792.name: Anvil Carrier
792.desc: A colossal anvil with a horn for a prow. Its face is a forge, and the sparks it throws are Ember Darts.

793.name: Splinter Interceptor
793.desc: Three needle shards in a forward arrowhead, flying in perfect formation with nothing holding them together but song.

794.name: Geode Freighter
794.desc: A rough dark geode split open along the top. The crystal inside is the hold, and it grows to fit whatever is carried in it.

795.name: Spire Dreadnought
795.desc: A mountain of crystal: one great spire and banks of shards radiating from it like frost on glass. Its shields are close to unbreakable, and its song can be heard through the hull of any ship in the system.

796.name: Kite Raider
796.desc: A small hull flown under a great diamond kite of patched canvas. Sarn raiders swoop on anyone who threatens a caravan, and then vanish downwind.

797.name: Ironwheel Destroyer
797.desc: A great armored wheel standing on its keel, a gun at every spoke. When it turns, it fires in every direction at once.

798.name: Polyp Dart
798.desc: A little glowing bell trailing four tentacles. Thalassi motherships release Polyps in clouds, like a reef spawning.

799.name: Nautilus Skiff
799.desc: A spiral shell with a tuft of tentacles at the mouth. Nautiluses carry Thalassi mail between the stars, and they never seem to run low on fuel.

800.name: Siphon Hauler
800.desc: A long sea-cucumber body carrying translucent cargo bladders. You can see the cargo sloshing about inside.

801.name: Manta Striker
801.desc: A flat diamond ray with a whip of a tail. Manta Strikers glide in low and fast, and their stingers leave a ship's systems twitching.

802.name: Ray Frigate
802.desc: A great ray with a dorsal ridge of glowing turret blisters. Rays travel in pairs and are fiercely protective of their young.

803.name: Medusa Cruiser
803.desc: A vast glowing bell with a frilled rim and a curtain of trailing tentacles, each one a stinger. It drifts, until it does not.

804.name: Abyssal Carrier
804.desc: An anglerfish the size of a station. Its lure is lit far ahead of it in the dark, and its glowing gills are hangars for clouds of Polyp Darts.

128.name: Mica Dart
128.desc: A compact charge-spool throws needlelike plasma darts; efficient against small shields.

129.name: Cinder Driver
129.desc: A staggered discharge chamber launches dense cinders for general-purpose ship combat.

130.name: Mica Sentinel
130.desc: A tracking charge-spool mount protects freighters without a large power budget.

131.name: Cinder Sentinel
131.desc: A stabilized cinder mount keeps steady pressure on fast shielded attackers.

132.name: Kiln Bastion
132.desc: A capital mount compresses a furnace charge into a slow, shield-breaking volley.

134.name: Skein Pursuer
134.desc: A pursuing microdrone follows an exhaust wake and detonates a shaped ceramic charge.

143.name: Spall Driver
143.desc: An armor-focused projector fractures a compact charge inside its forward tracking cone.

146.name: Prism Stitch
146.desc: A gated optical array stitches across shields at short range, with a mild systems shock.

156.name: Kestrel Needle
156.desc: A narrow-tracking induction cradle accelerates a light penetrator over long distances.

157.name: Harrier Needle
157.desc: A reinforced induction cradle trades agility for a denser armor penetrator.

158.name: Osprey Needle
158.desc: A heavy induction cradle launches deliberate, hard-hitting penetrators from the bow.

161.name: Chaffguard
161.desc: A rapid tracking mount sprays sacrificial flechettes through incoming missile paths.

162.name: Spall Crown
162.desc: An all-round pressure chamber sustains close-range armor-fracturing fire.

181.name: Seam Tapper
181.desc: A tuned stress pulse opens mineral seams; its focusing lattice is poor against shields.

197.name: Breakwater Array
197.desc: A rotating siege cradle drives massive penetrators across a capital engagement.

444.name: Sail Lance
444.desc: A Que'vari beam turret that focuses the light of a ship's own sails into a single unwavering lance.

445.name: Prism Shard Cannon
445.desc: Fires shards of hardened light cut by a prism the size of a fist. They ring like glass when they strike.

446.name: Corona Torpedo Tube
446.desc: Launches Corona torpedoes: knots of folded light that seek their target and unfold on impact.

447.name: Corona Torpedo
447.desc: Ammunition for the Corona Torpedo Tube.

448.name: Halo Burst Turret
448.desc: A ring of tiny emitters that swats incoming missiles and fighters out of the sky in bursts of light.

449.name: Mote Bay
449.desc: A cradle for Lumen Motes, the small sail-darts that Que'vari choirs send out like sparks.

450.name: Lumen Mote
450.desc: One Lumen Mote for your Mote Bay.

451.name: Electro-Sail Rig
451.desc: A spread of light-blue energy fabric rigged to your hull. It catches light the way a sail catches wind: better acceleration and speed.

452.name: Prism Ward
452.desc: Prism lattices woven through your shield emitters. Shields are stronger and recover faster.

453.name: Lightwell Core
453.desc: A small heart of captured starlight. It slowly refills your fuel tanks and holds two jumps more.

560.name: Reinforced Lattice I
560.desc: A bolt-on web of laminated spars that spreads impact loads across the hull. Cheap, heavy-ish, and the first thing any salvager installs. Each tier is a full replacement kit; the outfitter only stocks the next tier once you own the one before it.

561.name: Reinforced Lattice II
561.desc: Second-generation lattice with ceramic infill between the spars. Noticeably harder to punch through.

562.name: Reinforced Lattice III
562.desc: Foamed-titanium lattice cells. Yards in the core worlds sell this as standard on their gunboats.

563.name: Reinforced Lattice IV
563.desc: Self-knitting lattice: micro-seams slowly re-fuse after a hit, giving a trickle of armor regeneration.

564.name: Reinforced Lattice V
564.desc: The best plating money can buy outside a navy dockyard. Self-knitting seams and a dense honeycomb core.

565.name: Capacitor Bank I
565.desc: A rack of quick-discharge capacitors wired into your shield emitters. Each tier is a full replacement kit; the outfitter only stocks the next tier once you own the one before it.

566.name: Capacitor Bank II
566.desc: Doubles the rack with better cooling. Your shields stay up through one more volley.

567.name: Capacitor Bank III
567.desc: Graphene-plate capacitors that also help the emitters recover between hits.

568.name: Capacitor Bank IV
568.desc: Military-pattern banks with a dedicated recharge loop.

569.name: Capacitor Bank V
569.desc: Superconducting banks. Shields that shrug off what would have gutted you a year ago.

570.name: Thruster Retune I
570.desc: A dockside retune of your main thrusters: better acceleration and a little more top speed. Each tier is a full replacement kit; the outfitter only stocks the next tier once you own the one before it.

572.name: Thruster Retune III
572.desc: Replaces the injector manifold. Pilots say the ship feels lighter.

573.name: Thruster Retune IV
573.desc: Full racing tune. Loud, hot, and very, very quick.

574.name: Gyro Vane I
574.desc: Reaction-wheel vanes that sharpen your turn rate. Each tier is a full replacement kit; the outfitter only stocks the next tier once you own the one before it.

576.name: Gyro Vane III
576.desc: Cryo-cooled vanes. You will turn inside most fighters.

577.name: Cargo Compression I
577.desc: Rebuilds your hold racks to pack goods tighter. More cargo space, no extra outfit space used. Each tier is a full replacement kit; the outfitter only stocks the next tier once you own the one before it.

579.name: Cargo Compression III
579.desc: Variable-geometry hold. Freighter captains would sell their mothers for this.

580.name: Fuel Bladder I
580.desc: An expandable bladder tank tucked into dead hull space. Adds one jump of fuel. Each tier is a full replacement kit; the outfitter only stocks the next tier once you own the one before it.

581.name: Fuel Bladder II
581.desc: Larger bladder with baffles. Two extra jumps.

582.name: Fuel Bladder III
582.desc: Triple-walled bladder. Three extra jumps; explorers swear by it.

583.name: Solar Scoop
583.desc: Fold-out collector vanes that trickle hydrogen into your tanks while you fly. Slow, but it means you are never truly stranded.

584.name: Jump Plotter
584.desc: A navigation computer that chains up to three hyperspace jumps without stopping to recalculate.

585.name: Spool Accelerator
585.desc: Pre-spools your hyperdrive so you can jump the moment you clear a planet's gravity.

598.name: Ember Flak Turret
598.desc: A fast-cycling turret that throws a cone of glowing shrapnel. Good against fighters and incoming missiles.

599.name: Snare Projector
599.desc: An ion projector that overloads a target's systems instead of tearing it apart. Salvagers love it, and so do pirates.

600.name: Wisp Rocket Pod
600.desc: A four-tube pod of small seeking rockets.

601.name: Wisp Rocket
601.desc: Ammunition for the Wisp Rocket Pod.

602.name: Mite Drone Bay
602.desc: A launch rack for Mite drones: tiny, fearless fighters that swarm your target.

603.name: Mite Drone
603.desc: One Mite drone for your drone bay.

604.name: Lantern Lance
604.desc: A Lamplighter beam projector. Its light is the color of a hearth seen through rain.

605.name: Phase Veil
605.desc: A cloaking field that slips your ship half a step out of phase with the rest of the universe. Drains fuel quickly while active.

606.name: Blink Thrusters
606.desc: Quantum-tunneling thruster cores. Hit the afterburner and the ship seems to skip forward between frames.

608.name: Quantum Capacitor
608.desc: A capacitor that stores charge in superposition. Your shields come back before you have finished flinching.

609.name: Superposition Hull
609.desc: Hull plating that exists in two states at once: intact, and very slightly less intact. It slowly repairs itself toward the first one.

610.name: Quantum Spool
610.desc: Spools your hyperdrive in every possible state at once. Instant jump-out and up to four jumps in a row.

611.name: Quantum Torpedo Tube
611.desc: Launches seeking torpedoes that tunnel through point-defense fire.

612.name: Quantum Torpedo
612.desc: Ammunition for the Quantum Torpedo Tube.

613.name: Drift Mine Layer
613.desc: Drops proximity mines behind your ship. Pursuers learn to give you room.

614.name: Drift Mine
614.desc: A proximity mine for the Drift Mine Layer.

615.name: Cutter Beam
615.desc: A short salvage-cutting beam. Shreds armor and asteroids, but barely tickles shields.
